newsitem.title: USA: Republicans committed to balanced US budget--Armey.
newsitem.headline: Republicans committed to balanced US budget--Armey.

text.p: House Majority Leader Richard Armey said on Tuesday that President Clinton's plan to balance the budget by 2002 was not credible, but underscored that Republicans were still committed to getting a balanced budget deal this year.
Armey told reporters new Congressional Budget Office figures showing Clinton's budget fell $69 billion short of balance in 2002 were troubling, saying the president should submit a revised plan.

"We intend to get to a balanced budget, we want to work with the president to do that," Armey said. "We will get a balanced bduget, we need a balanced budget. We will work on it and try to get agreement."
He said White House officials were forthcoming in private meetings, telling Republican leaders they were committed to balancing the budget and wanted to address any problems.

Armey tried to sidestep questions about whether Republicans would craft their own budget if they could not work out an acceptable proposal with Clinton. Asked whether Republicans would go solo if the two sides couldn't work together he said, "I reckon."
He said the two sides had to avoid repeating partisan budget battles, saying "staring at each other across the table or across Pennsylvania Avenue with a double dare" was unproductive.
